# Ezekiel 16 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** The LORD's message came to me again:

**2** "Son of man, confront Jerusalem with her disgusting sins.

**3** Tell her: This is what the Lord GOD says to Jerusalem: You come from the land of Canaan. Your father was an Amorite and your mother was a Hittite.

**4** On the day you were born, no one cut your umbilical cord. No one washed you or rubbed you with salt or wrapped you in cloths.

**5** No one cared enough to do any of these things for you. No one had pity on you. You were thrown out into an open field, because on the day you were born, you were despised.

**6** But I came by and saw you lying there in your blood. And I said to you as you lay in your blood, 'Live!' Yes, I said to you, 'Live!'

**7** I helped you thrive like a wildflower. You grew up and became a beautiful young woman. Your figure filled out and your hair grew long, but you were still naked and bare.

**8** When I passed by again and saw you, you were old enough for love. So I spread my cloak over you to cover your nakedness. I made a solemn vow and entered into a covenant with you, declares the Lord GOD, and you became Mine.

**9** I bathed you, washed the blood from you, and rubbed fragrant oil on your skin.

**10** I dressed you in embroidered clothes and fine leather sandals. I wrapped you in linen and draped you in silk.

**11** I gave you jewelry — bracelets for your wrists, a necklace for your neck,

**12** a ring for your nose, earrings for your ears, and a magnificent crown for your head.

**13** You were adorned with gold and silver. Your clothes were fine linen, silk, and embroidery. You ate the finest flour, honey, and olive oil. You grew more and more beautiful, and you rose to be a queen.

**14** Your fame spread among the nations because of your beauty — which was perfect, because I had made you stunning with the splendor I gave you, declares the Lord GOD.

**15** But you trusted in your own beauty. You used your fame to become a prostitute, giving yourself to every man who passed by.

**16** You used your beautiful gifts to build pagan shrines and gave yourself to prostitution — outrageous acts that should never have happened.

**35** So listen up, you prostitute — hear the word of the LORD!

**36** The Lord GOD says: Because you poured out your lust, exposed yourself to your lovers, worshiped disgusting idols, and even sacrificed your children's blood to them —

**37** I am going to gather all those lovers you enjoyed — both the ones you loved and the ones you hated. I will gather them against you from every side and strip you naked in front of them all.

**44** Everyone will quote this proverb about you: 'Like mother, like daughter.'

**45** Your 'sisters' Sodom and Samaria didn't do half of what you've done. You've committed so many horrible sins that you make them look righteous by comparison.

**53** But I will restore the fortunes of Sodom and Samaria and their surrounding villages — and I will restore your fortunes too, right along with them.

**54** You will bear your shame and be humiliated by everything you've done — especially since your sins actually made your sisters look decent by comparison.

**59** The Lord GOD says: I will treat you the way you deserve, because you broke our covenant and despised the vows you made.

**60** But I will remember the covenant I made with you when you were young, and I will establish an everlasting covenant with you.

**61** Then you will remember what you've done and be ashamed — especially when I give you Sodom and Samaria as your sisters, as daughters, even though this was not part of our original covenant.

**62** I will reestablish My covenant with you, and you will know that I am the LORD.

**63** Then you will remember and be so ashamed that you will never open your mouth to make excuses again — because I will forgive you for everything you have done, declares the Lord GOD."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **16:4-6**: The image is heartbreaking — a newborn baby thrown into a field, still covered in blood, with no one to care. God walks by, sees this unwanted child, and says one word: 'Live.' That's the origin story of Jerusalem.

- **16:15**: Everything beautiful Jerusalem had was a gift from God. But she took those gifts and used them to chase other lovers. The problem with beauty is that it can become the basis for independence from the One who gave it.

- **16:60-63**: After 59 verses of the most devastating indictment in Scripture, God says: 'But I will remember.' He'll establish an everlasting covenant. The shame won't be erased — but it will be forgiven. Grace gets the last word.

— PNEUMA
